teaching.causalExplanation: Start with the speed. Work is done only by the part of a force along the direction of motion. The magnetic force is always at right angles to the velocity, so it has no part along the motion, and it does no work, at any instant. No work means no change in kinetic energy, so the speed stays exactly the same. The field changes the direction of the velocity, never its size. That's different from the electric field between plates, which pushed partly along the motion, did work, and sped the electron up. So the speed is constant, which means the force, q v B, has a constant size too. A force of constant size, always at right angles to the velocity, turns the path by the same amount every moment. That's uniform circular motion, which we've met before. The magnetic force points to the centre of the circle. It is the centripetal force. There's no extra force, and nothing at the centre. Set the magnetic force equal to the centripetal force the circle needs. q v B equals m v squared over r. One v cancels, so r equals m v over q B. Read what it says. A faster or heavier particle swings out on a bigger circle. A stronger field, or a bigger charge, pulls it into a tighter one. The mass is on top because a heavier particle is harder to turn.

- **Learner question (route wording kept).** "Why does a perpendicular magnetic field bend a path without increasing speed?" - **Worked example (site card 3, exact numbers).** Electron r = 1.14 mm, proton r = 2.09 m (ratio 1837); periods 1.79 ns and 3.28 μs. Opposite senses of rotation (electron clockwise? see author note b for the sense in the drawn field).
- **Cyclotron.** Named in one clause as the use of the speed-independent period, with the necessary condition "well below the speed of light" kept in learner copy, because without it the claim is wrong.
- **Comparison with other circular motion (`P6-IQ1-04`, ACSPH108; site card 4 and "Compare 5 marks").** Three systems, one rule (real force = mv²/r): ball on a string (tension adjusts; the string fixes r), satellite (gravity; faster orbit is smaller, r = GM/v²), charge in B (force set by v; faster takes a bigger circle). Plates: steel ball (m5-v11), Earth and satellite (m5-v17).
- **Comparison with an electric field (`P6-IQ1-04`).** One scene: parabola and changing speed against circle and constant speed. v06 develops the force-by-force comparison.
- **Out of scope by design (site "oblique entry" box).** Helical motion is not narrated (author note c).
- **Memory aid.** "A magnetic force steers; it never speeds." Plus "r = mv/qB: momentum on top, charge and field underneath." See "Memory aid check".

  (a) Work: P = F · v = 0 at every instant, so K is constant exactly (not just on average).
  (b) Senses of rotation in the drawn field (B into the page, viewer looking at the page): a positive charge moving right is pushed up, so it circulates anticlockwise; an electron circulates clockwise. Checked with F = q(v × B).

Main question: *A proton moves through a magnetic field, pushed sideways at every instant. The push never stops, so why doesn't it speed up, what path does it follow, and how big is the loop?*
Entry knowledge: v04; m5-v11; v02, v03.
Stops after: zero work and constant speed; the circle; r = mv/(qB); T = 2πm/(qB); comparisons with other circular motion and with an electric field. No combined fields.

- **No video numbers on screen.** Where a Visual line tags something with a video code, the on-screen words say "last time", "an earlier video" or "next time". Video codes in this document are notes for the builder.

scenes.teachingReason: How long does one lap take? The period is the distance round, two pi r, over the speed. Put in r equals m v over q B, and the v cancels, so T equals two pi m over q B. That's surprising. A faster particle goes round a bigger circle, in exactly the same time. For the electron here, one lap takes one point seven nine nanoseconds. For the proton, three point two eight microseconds. This is what lets a cyclotron keep particles in step, as long as they stay well below the speed of light.

scenes.teachingReason: Let's compare this with other circular motion. In every case, a real force supplies m v squared over r. For a ball whirled on a string, the tension adjusts, and the string fixes the radius. For a satellite, gravity supplies the force, and a faster orbit is a smaller one, r equals big G M over v squared. For a charge in a magnetic field, the force is set by the speed, and a faster particle takes a bigger circle. Same rule, three different causes.
